question: Does an individual's other-night vertical rule predict a target session better than other bats observed during the same calendar night?

night_definition.rule: UTC timestamp shifted backward by 12 hours, then calendar date
night_definition.rationale: keeps evening-to-next-morning nocturnal tracks in one start-night bin without using outcome values

semantics.height_true: height above ground level from 30 m ASTER DEM
semantics.height-above-msl: GPS height above mean sea level

predictors.self: equal-session P(z|x,y) from the same bat's other sessions
predictors.same_night_other: equal-individual P(z|x,y) from other bats on the target calendar night

interpretation.positive: cross-night individual identity predicts vertical state better than contemporaneous other bats, arguing against calendar-night environment as the sole explanation
interpretation.nonpositive: night-specific shared context is at least as predictive as individual history

claim_boundary: Post-primary context control; cannot alter the frozen MSL/AGL self-transfer endpoints.
